questions: Can the subgraph be any subset of vertices and edges of T, or must it be an induced subgraph (i.e., must include all edges of T whose endpoints are both selected)?
When selecting a subgraph, are isolated vertices (degree 0) allowed, or must every selected vertex have degree exactly 1 or 4 within the subgraph?
If multiple subgraphs achieve the maximum size, does the output need to specify which one, or is only the size sufficient?
Should the answer be -1 only when no subgraph with at least one vertex satisfies the degree conditions, or also when the only possible subgraph is a single vertex of degree 0?
Are vertices of degree 4 required to have exactly four distinct neighbors within the subgraph, or can multiple edges to the same neighbor count (i.e., multigraph considerations are irrelevant)?
Is the tree guaranteed to be connected, and does the subgraph also need to be connected (i.e., a tree itself), or can it consist of multiple disconnected components?
Are there any constraints on the size of the subgraph beyond the degree conditions, such as requiring the subgraph to contain at least one leaf (degree‑1 vertex)?
In the output, should the answer be printed as a plain integer followed by a newline, and is any extra whitespace or formatting (e.g., trailing spaces) allowed?
answers: Not specified beyond what's given; assume the subgraph must be induced, i.e. contain all edges of T whose endpoints are both selected.
Not specified beyond what's given; every selected vertex must have degree exactly 1 or 4 within the subgraph, so isolated vertices are not allowed.
Not specified beyond what's given; only the size of the largest alkane subgraph is needed, not which specific one.
The output should be -1 whenever no valid alkane subgraph -- one containing at least one degree-4 vertex -- exists; a subgraph with only degree-0 vertices does not qualify.
Not specified beyond what's given; multigraph considerations are irrelevant here since the input is a simple tree.
Not specified beyond what's given; assume the subgraph must remain a single connected tree.
Not specified beyond what's given; the alkane definition only requires degree 1 or 4 with at least one degree-4 vertex, with no separate leaf requirement stated.
Not specified beyond what's given; a standard integer with a trailing newline is expected.
inline_prompts: You are given an undirected tree T with N vertices, numbered 1, 2, \ldots, N. The i-th edge is an undirected edge connecting vertices A_i and B_i. A graph is defined to be an alkane if and only if it satisfies the following conditions: - The graph is an undirected tree. - Every vertex has degree 1 or 4. Determine whether there exists a subgraph of T that is an alkane, and if so, find the maximum number of vertices in such a subgraph. Input The input is given from Standard Input in the following format: N A_1 B_1 A_2 B_2 \vdots A_{N - 1} B_{N - 1} Output If there exists a subgraph of T that is an alkane, print the answer. Otherwise, print -1. Constraints - 1 \leq N \leq 2 \times 10^5 - 1 \leq A_i, B_i \leq N - The given graph is an undirected tree. - All input values are integers.
